# dlansy

> Return the value of the one-norm, Frobenius norm, infinity-norm, or the largest absolute value of any element of a real symmetric matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var dlansy = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dlansy' );
```

#### dlansy( order, norm, uplo, N, A, LDA )

Returns the value of the specified norm of a real symmetric matrix `A`.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var A = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 5.0 ] );

var v = dlansy( 'row-major', 'M', 'upper', 2, A, 2 );
// returns 5.0
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **order**: storage layout.
-   **norm**: specifies the norm type (`'M'`/`'m'`: max norm, `'1'`/`'O'`/`'o'`: one norm, `'I'`/`'i'`: infinity norm, `'F'`/`'f'`/`'E'`/`'e'`: Frobenius norm).
-   **uplo**: specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of `A` is referenced (`'upper'` or `'lower'`).
-   **N**: order of the matrix `A`. When `N = 0`, the function returns `0`.
-   **A**: input [`Float64Array`][@stdlib/array/float64] containing the symmetric matrix.
-   **LDA**: stride of the first dimension of `A` (a.k.a., leading dimension of the matrix `A`).

Note that indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use [`typed array`][mdn-typed-array] views.

<!-- eslint-disable stdlib/capitalized-comments -->

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

// Initial array...
var A0 = new Float64Array( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 5.0 ] );

// Create an offset view...
var A1 = new Float64Array( A0.buffer, A0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );

var v = dlansy( 'row-major', 'M', 'upper', 2, A1, 2 );
// returns 5.0
```

#### dlansy.ndarray( norm, uplo, N, A, sa1, sa2, oa )

Returns the value of the specified norm of a real symmetric matrix `A` using alternative indexing semantics.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var A = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 5.0 ] );

var v = dlansy.ndarray( 'M', 'upper', 2, A, 2, 1, 0 );
// returns 5.0
```

The function has the following additional parameters:

-   **sa1**: stride of the first dimension of `A`.
-   **sa2**: stride of the second dimension of `A`.
-   **oa**: starting index for `A`.

While [`typed array`][mdn-typed-array] views mandate a view offset based on the underlying buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on starting indices. For example,

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var A = new Float64Array( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 5.0 ] );

var v = dlansy.ndarray( 'M', 'upper', 2, A, 2, 1, 1 );
// returns 5.0
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlansy()` corresponds to the [LAPACK][lapack] routine [`dlansy`][lapack-dlansy].
-   Since the matrix is symmetric, the one norm and infinity norm are equal.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/to-array' );
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform' );
var shape2strides = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/shape2strides' );
var dlansy = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dlansy' );

var shape = [ 3, 3 ];
var order = 'row-major';
var strides = shape2strides( shape, order );

var A = uniform( 9, -10, 10, {
    'dtype': 'float64'
});
console.log( ndarray2array( A, shape, strides, 0, order ) );

var v = dlansy( order, 'M', 'upper', shape[ 0 ], A, strides[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'Max norm:', v );

v = dlansy( order, '1', 'upper', shape[ 0 ], A, strides[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'One norm:', v );

v = dlansy( order, 'F', 'upper', shape[ 0 ], A, strides[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'Frobenius norm:', v );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
